A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, central approach and retained experiments. All 16 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison; no essential material is unreadable.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original output-distribution experiments on Diabetes, Iris and Wine. The examples and Appendix C additionally report Beta-input distribution estimation and tanh-network approximation experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report revised experiments, including Banana, additional Diabetes perturbations and runtime measurements. The original Iris case studies remain in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 refines the stated segmentation rule to include discontinuities in the first or second derivative. The underlying IBP, interpolation/tangent bounds, ReLU conversion and sign-aware layer composition remain. Algorithm 1 primarily formalizes existing steps rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation of a Banana-trained network under Gaussian input perturbations and extends Diabetes testing from one perturbed feature to two. These modestly expand the existing output-CDF task. Iris, Wine and the Beta-input Iris examples remain.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain Monte Carlo and PLT; both also participate in the added experiments. The appendix Iris comparison retains Gaussian KDE and the sampled histogram. PROVEN and other verification methods remain related work rather than evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 substantially revises the reported Diabetes evaluation: test cases increase from 73 to 133 and CDF evaluation points from 20 to 1000. Runtime measurement is added across comparisons, alongside the new Banana experiment. The stated 70/30 split and 100-million-sample main Monte Carlo budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new runtime columns provide computational-cost comparisons across input dimensions, and the two-feature Diabetes experiment extends perturbation testing. The existing five-versus-ten-segment tanh approximation analysis and Iris KDE/Monte Carlo case study are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 replaces v1's ambiguously labelled parenthetical out-of-bounds summaries with explicit minimum/median/maximum counts across test cases. Bound widths retain mean/standard-deviation reporting. This changes reporting of between-case variability, without establishing additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces bound-width and out-of-bounds results throughout and adds Banana, two-feature Diabetes and timings. For Iris with 50% deletion and three uncertain inputs, mean bound width changes from 0.06864 to 0.2019. New two-feature Diabetes runtimes are 504 seconds for PLT and 4.0 seconds for the proposed method. These are revised or newly reported results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.11 broadens the existence result to continuous activations and removes the fixed-depth promise, with a new UAT-based proof. Definition 3.12, Theorem 3.14 and Appendix B add piecewise-C2 assumptions and detailed approximation/composition proofs, replacing v1's brief sketch. The UDAT is retained as Theorem 3.16. However, new Theorems B.6–B.7 use max f'' without absolute values, invalidating their stated error bounds for concave functions.

C1.justification: The central exact-integration, guaranteed-bound, convergence and UDAT contributions remain. The abstract, contribution 4 and conclusion narrow constructive applicability from monotonic piecewise differentiable activations to monotonic piecewise twice continuously differentiable activations. The introduction also qualifies the comparator violations as occurring where bounds are tight.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the 50,000-vertex cap produces wider bounds in higher dimensions, qualifying v1's general emphasis on frequent comparator violations. It also distinguishes the general existence theorem from the practical construction. Existing compact-support and larger-network limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly discloses PLT subdivision counts of 250/100/30, the proposed implementation's 50,000-vertex cap, and Gaussian-mixture construction through KDE on MICE imputations. It also specifies Banana's two 16-neuron hidden layers and data source. These disclosures do not establish that previously undocumented settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Delaunay, Driscoll and Braun, Rudin, and the Banana dataset source. The positioning against PLT, PROVEN and verification research remains largely intact. Most other bibliography changes update publication details or consolidate duplicate references.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is locally expanded and reorganized to distinguish existence and constructive guarantees, alongside language and terminology edits. Impact and acknowledgments sections are added. The new proof appendix shifts the retained subnetwork and Iris appendices from B/C to C/D; the main section sequence remains.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned with grouped out-of-bounds summaries, runtime columns and revised dataset labels. Algorithm 1 adds a pseudocode display, Figure 2 is enlarged and relocated, and Figure 3 gains an overall caption. The six existing figures retain their substantive graphical content, with appendix placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical transparency through refinement-budget disclosures, clearer statistical summaries, runtime comparisons and explanation of wider bounds at higher dimensions. Separating existence from constructive guarantees also clarifies the theory. However, the new error bounds in Theorems B.6–B.7 fail for concave functions because their constants omit absolute values. These defects limit the benefit of the expanded proofs, leaving a modest overall improvement.
